privacy.title: Privacy & security
privacy.description: What is stored, where, and what leaves your computer.
privacy.modeDescription: Blurs amounts and numbers on screen, for example while screen sharing or in a cafe. You can also turn it on from the button at the bottom of the menu.
privacy.protectShort: Encrypt your disk and keep backups encrypted.
privacy.storedDescription: Everything stays on this computer. No account, no cloud.
privacy.storedTransactions: Transactions, categories, budgets and goals - in the database file (penny.db).
privacy.storedCredentials: Bank logins, the AI provider API key and the bot token - encrypted with AES-256-GCM.
privacy.storedKey: The encryption key - in .encryption-key in the same folder, readable only by your user.
privacy.storedSettings: Display preferences such as privacy mode and the collapsed menu - in the browser only.
privacy.leavesDescription: Only what you turned on, and only to these places.
privacy.leavesBanks: Banks and card companies - your login goes only to the bank's own site, during a sync.

privacy.leavesUpdate: Update check against GitHub - none of your data, only whether a new version exists.
privacy.protectBody: Turn on disk encryption (BitLocker on Windows, FileVault on Mac). Anyone who can read the data folder can read your transactions. A backup of the folder includes the encryption key - keep it somewhere encrypted.
privacy.deleteDescription: Delete transactions or fully reset the app, on the Accounts & import page.
privacy.lockDescription: Asks for a passphrase to open the app and locks after idle time. The encryption key is stored wrapped with the passphrase, so a copy of the data folder does not expose bank logins. After a restart, unlock once so scheduled sync and the bot can work. Forgot it? The only way back is to delete everything.
privacy.lockHint: At least 8 characters, or a PIN of 6 or more digits.

privacy.lockError_weak: Too short: at least 8 characters, or a 6-digit PIN.

legacy.defaultSteps:
Breathe. No big money decisions are needed in the first weeks.
Get several copies of the death certificate.
Contact the banks and card companies with the death certificate, and later with the inheritance or probate order.
Check Har HaKesef (Ministry of Finance) for pension, provident and study funds.
Check Har HaBituach for insurance policies, and contact the insurers.
Notify Bituach Leumi and ask about survivors' benefits.
Go over recurring charges and cancel subscriptions that are no longer needed.
Ask the accountant or lawyer about an inheritance or probate order.

retireTools.trackIntro: Three short questions and the kinds of track worth checking first. In a pension, provident or study fund you can switch track inside the same fund, tax-free, without changing company.
retireTools.riskLabel: Your savings drop 20%. What do you do?
retireTools.risk_low_hint: A steady balance matters to you. A calmer track helps you not sell at the worst time.
retireTools.risk_mid_hint: Drops are uncomfortable, but you leave the money alone. Most people are here.
retireTools.risk_high_hint: Drops look like a sale to you. Over the long run that helps, if it holds on a bad day too.
retireTools.trackHead: {years} years to retirement. Tracks to check, in order:
retireTools.track_sp500_why: Broad spread over the largest US companies, usually with low external management costs. Volatile, and exposed to the dollar rate.
retireTools.track_stocks_why: Mostly local and global shares, picked by the fund. Suits a long horizon and someone who can sit through drops.
retireTools.track_ageBased_why: The default in most funds: it lowers risk by itself as you age (up to 50, 50 to 60, 60 and over). Good if you'd rather not think about it.
retireTools.track_general_why: A mix of shares and bonds. Gentler swings, lower expected return.
retireTools.track_bonds_why: For money you need soon. Small swings, low expected return.
retireTools.track_selfManaged_why: You pick the securities yourself inside the fund and keep the tax benefits. You pay the fund's fee plus trading and custody fees at the broker, so it pays off mainly with a larger balance and the will to manage it.
retireTools.fees1: Fees are set per fund, not per track. You can usually move to an index track without paying more.
retireTools.fees2: Index tracks usually carry lower external management costs. The annual report shows them as direct expenses.
retireTools.fees3: Self-managed adds broker fees. On a small balance they can swallow the advantage.
retireTools.chIntro: The pension clearing house lists every pension fund, managers' insurance policy, provident fund and study fund in your name in one report. For individuals it is a snapshot to read, not a file to import, so you copy over a few numbers. It takes about fifteen minutes.
retireTools.step1_body: On the clearing-house site, identify with your ID number and ask for a one-off report on all products. There is a small fee, and it usually arrives within one to three business days.
retireTools.step2_body: For each product: the type, the company, the balance, the monthly deposit, the fees from deposit and from balance, and the track. For a pension fund, also the disability cover percentage and whether survivors are covered.
retireTools.step3_body: On the Investments page, add each fund as an asset with its balance, deposit and fees. Link it to the public data to compare it with similar funds.
retireTools.step4_body: Compare your fees with the market and check disability and survivor cover below. An old fund with a small balance and no deposits is worth checking for merging into your active one.
retireTools.coverIntro: A comprehensive pension fund includes disability and survivor insurance. The figures are in the clearing-house report and the fund's annual report.
retireTools.f_dependents: Does anyone depend on your income?
retireTools.cover_disabilityLow: Disability cover is below 75% of salary, the full level in pension funds. If you can't work, income drops sharply. You can ask the fund to raise it.
retireTools.cover_disabilityOk: Disability cover is at the full level.
retireTools.cover_survivorsMissing: Someone depends on you, but survivors aren't covered. Check with the fund whether you waived it in the past, and renew.
retireTools.cover_survivorsMaybeWaive: No one depends on you, yet you pay for survivor cover. You can ask to waive it for a limited period and save the cost, then renew when things change.
retireTools.cover_survivorsOk: Survivor cover matches what you marked.

calculators.annuity_q: Take a monthly annuity or a lump sum?
calculators.annuity_explain: Annuity = balance divided by the conversion factor, for life. Lump sum = the amount after tax, invested and drawn in equal payments until the age you pick, then it runs out. A pension fund lets you commute only part of the pension; the choice is made with the fund and the Tax Authority (form 161d).

lostMoney.title: Forgotten money
lostMoney.hint: Find old savings and accounts, and decide what to do with each.
lostMoney.intro: Anyone who has worked in a few places often has small funds they forgot. The official search is free and takes a few minutes.
lostMoney.step_search: Search pension savings and life policies
lostMoney.step_search_why: On the government site, with national ID login. It shows which companies hold an account for you, without balances.
lostMoney.step_banks_why: Same site, banks section. It lists banks holding an inactive account or deposit in your name.
lostMoney.step_list_why: The company and the kind of saving. Ask the company itself for the balance.
lostMoney.step_decide: Decide for each: merge, move or claim
lostMoney.step_decide_why: The tool below suggests an action per kind. Contact the company directly, usually through its personal area.
lostMoney.step_fees: Check what's left isn't paying high fees
lostMoney.step_fees_why: An account with no deposits keeps paying management fees, and usually nobody negotiates them.
lostMoney.foundHint: Add each finding to get a suggested action. The list isn't saved.
lostMoney.hasActive: I have an active pension fund today (receiving deposits)
lostMoney.action_merge_how: Ask your active fund to absorb the old one. You pay fees in one place and keep insurance continuity.
lostMoney.action_move_how: Transfer it to a fund you choose, with low fees and an investment track that suits your age. A matured study fund can also be withdrawn.
lostMoney.action_claim_how: Contact the bank or insurer with ID. For a relative who died, you'll also need inheritance documents.
lostMoney.feesTitle: Why not leave it as is
lostMoney.feesBody: An inactive fund keeps charging management fees on the balance, and the insurance cover in an old pension fund may lapse after a while without deposits. Small balances are sometimes merged automatically, but don't count on it.
lostMoney.scamBody: The government search is free. Anyone offering to find lost money for a cut usually does what you can do yourself in minutes.
lostMoney.notAdvice: General information, an estimate, not advice. Before moving or withdrawing, check tax and terms with the managing company.

rights.localAuthority: Each local authority sets its own discounts. Look for the property-tax discount page on your city or council site.
rights.estimate: An estimate, not advice. Amounts, caps and terms change every year.
rights.r_workGrant_why: A yearly top-up for low-wage workers who are parents or 55+. It isn't paid automatically: you file a claim, also for past years.
rights.r_reserveTax: Tax credit points for reserve duty
rights.r_reserveTax_why: From 30 service days a year you get credit points, more for longer service. Claimed through your employer with an IDF eligibility form.
rights.r_reserveGrant_why: From 40 service days a year there are extra grants, plus benefits for students, parents and the self-employed. Worth going through the full list.
rights.r_childAllowance_why: Paid for each child up to 18, usually automatically. Check the number of children and bank details are right.
rights.r_childSavings_why: A monthly deposit in each child's name. You can double it from the allowance and pick a provident fund over a bank; over 18 years the gap can be large.
rights.r_arnona_why: Local authorities give discounts by income, age, disability or family status. It isn't automatic: you apply.
rights.r_rent_why: Monthly help from the Housing Ministry for renters who meet its conditions. Applying online is free.
rights.r_unemployment_why: After a job ends, for those with enough months of work. Register with the Employment Service first, and don't wait.

st.title: Accessibility statement
st.intro: This app is built to be usable by everyone, including people with disabilities. This statement describes what we did, what is still missing, and how to reach us.
st.standardBody: This app follows Israeli Standard IS 5568 (based on WCAG 2.0) at level AA, as required by the Equal Rights for Persons with Disabilities Law, 1998, and the Equal Rights for Persons with Disabilities (Service Accessibility Adjustments) Regulations, 2013. We aim for WCAG 2.2 level AA.
st.done1: Every page works with a keyboard alone, with a “Skip to content” link and a visible focus outline.
st.done2: Buttons, fields and icons have names screen readers announce; pages use headings and landmarks.
st.done3: Hebrew pages read right to left and English left to right, with the page language set correctly.
st.done4: Text and controls meet contrast requirements in light and dark themes.
st.done5: Animations respect the system “reduce motion” setting and can be stopped from the menu.
st.done6: Dialogs keep focus inside while open and return it when closed; notifications are announced.
st.done7: Pages work when zoomed to 200% and on narrow phone screens.
st.menuBody: Open it with the accessibility button (in the side menu, or the top bar on phones), with Alt+A, or from Settings › Accessibility. It offers: text size, high contrast (light or dark), wider spacing, a readable font, highlighted links and headings, a big cursor, stopping animations, a strong focus outline, hiding images and a reading guide. Choices are saved for each profile.
st.limits1: Charts show trends visually; the key figures also appear as text next to them, but not every chart point has a text equivalent.
st.limits2: Bank and card-company websites you sign in to are run by those companies and are outside our control.
st.limits3: Some small fixed-size labels in the budget view don't grow with the menu's text size; browser zoom enlarges them.
st.limits4: Text written by the AI assistant may be less structured than the rest of the app.
st.supportBody: This app is designed for current versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, and for screen readers such as NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver and TalkBack.
st.contactBody: Found something hard to use? Tell us what page, what you tried, and which browser or assistive technology you use.
